title: Discrete Choice with Generalized Social Interactions
abstract: arXiv:2610.27324v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper studies social interactions in discrete choice models in which individuals can respond differently to different network members, conforming to some while distinguishing from others. In this generalized framework, I show how to use within-network variation in individual choices to draw inference about differences in endogenous interaction effects, while accounting for unobserved contextual effects. I also show how to construct internal instruments to correct for measurement error bias, a key source of endogeneity in network models with incomplete information. I apply these results to data from two empirical settings: classroom peer effects in Tennessee primary schools and spillovers in deworming treatment uptake in Kenya. translated_title: 具有广义社会互动的离散选择模型
translated_abstract: 本文研究了离散选择模型中的社会互动问题，其中个体可以对不同的网络成员做出不同的反应，即与某些成员趋同而与另一些成员保持差异。在这一广义框架下，作者展示了如何利用网络内个体选择的变异来推断内生互动效应的差异，同时考虑未观察到的情境效应。此外，作者还展示了如何构建内部工具变量来纠正测量误差偏差，而测量误差是信息不完全的网络模型中内生性的一个关键来源。作者将这些方法应用于两个实证场景的数据：田纳西州小学的课堂同伴效应以及肯尼亚驱虫治疗采纳中的溢出效应。在这两个应用中，作者发现社会互动效应的差异——即个体对相似同伴表现出更强的趋同——在塑造人们的选择中起着关键作用。
tldr: 本文提出了一个允许个体对不同网络成员分别趋同或区分的广义社会互动离散选择模型，通过利用网络内选择变异识别内生互动效应差异，并构建内部工具变量纠正测量误差偏差，实证发现个体对相似同伴更强的趋同效应是塑造人们选择的关键因素。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a generalized social interactions discrete choice model where individuals can conform to some network members while distinguishing from others, shows how to identify differences in endogenous interaction effects using within-network choice variation and construct internal instruments to correct measurement error bias, and finds empirically that stronger conformity to similar peers plays a key role in shaping individuals' choices.
